items.originalTitle: Masked dirt bike riders swarm SUV in brazen NYC street attack, sparking police crackdown
items.title: Masked dirt bike riders swarm SUV in brazen NYC street attack, sparking police crackdown
items.summary: New York City officials are warning a group of masked dirt bike riders that arrests could be imminent after video captured a chaotic confrontation in which several riders surrounded and attacked a vehicle on a busy Staten Island street. The crackdown follows a Wednesday incident on Richmond Avenue in Staten Island's Bulls Head neighborhood, where video showed several masked riders swarming a white SUV stopped at a traffic light. In the video obtained by Fox News Digital, several individuals appeared to kick and strike the vehicle, while another appeared to throw an object at it. As the driver attempted to leave, the SUV appeared to run over a dirt bike that had been positioned in front of the vehicle. WATCH: E-BIKE TEEN TAKEOVER SWARMS DOWNTOWN CITY STREETS BLOCKING TRAFFIC, LEADING TO CHARGES During a news conference Thursday, NYPD Assistant Chief John Buttacavoli warned those involved that police were gathering intelligence and working to identify the suspects. "We know who you are, and you will be getting a knock on your door very soon," Buttacavoli said, emphasizing that the behavior had escalated from a quality-of-life concern into criminal activity. "It stops here. We're taking action," he added. Staten Island District Attorney Michael McMahon also condemned the riders, accusing them of intimidating motorists and putting innocent people at risk. VIDEO SHOWS BRIDGE TURN INTO BURNOUT BONANZA IN STUNT-HAPPY TAKEOVER – POLICE SWOOP IN TO CUFF ROAD REBELS "Like a plague of locusts, they descend upon drivers who are just going about their business here on Staten Island," McMahon said. "They're jackals, they're teenage terrorists, and it's not going to be tolerated here in our borough." McMahon called the behavior "simply outrageous," adding that no one had been seriously injured, based on the information available to officials. Wednesday's incident was part of a broader pattern of dangerous behavior involving motorized bikes , according to Staten Island Borough President Vito Fossella. Fossella described the riders as a "bunch of punks who are literally terrorizing drivers" as motorists went about their daily routines. "Enough. This game is over," Fossella said. The borough president also warned parents that their children were putting innocent motorists at risk. CITIES FEARING HALLOWEEN MAYHEM PUT TEENS ON NOTICE, ANNOUNCE CURFEWS AND CRACKDOWNS AFTER VIOLENT TAKEOVERS "Your kid is terrorizing innocent people when they're just going about their business. It's wrong, and it needs to stop," Fossella said. McMahon warned that parents could face legal or financial consequences if their children use illegal motorized vehicles to intimidate or injure others, including potential civil liability if someone is hurt. "Parents also must take responsibility for their children," McMahon's office said in a separate statement. Police have assembled a task force to address the problem and will continue confiscating illegally operated motorized bikes , according to Buttacavoli. He said officers had already identified several individuals and seized numerous bikes this year. GRINNING SUSPECT CUFFED AFTER ALLEGED FIERY STREET TAKEOVER, DRAG RACE CAUGHT ON CAMERA The NYPD also reminded residents that certain motorized vehicles must be registered, insured and operated by licensed drivers. State Assemblyman Mike Reilly, R-Staten Island, said he plans to introduce legislation in January that would hold parents financially responsible for minors caught recklessly operating certain motorized vehicles, according to the New York Post. The proposal would impose fines ranging from $250 to $1,500, the paper reported. The incident remains under investigation, and no arrests have been announced.

items.originalTitle: Benches clear in chaotic postgame brawl after Louisville Cardinals top North Carolina Tar Heels
items.title: Benches clear in chaotic postgame brawl after Louisville Cardinals top North Carolina Tar Heels
items.summary: The Louisville Cardinals managed to beat the North Carolina Tar Heels 16-14 after a late interception ended UNC's hopes of taking the lead. While that sounds exciting, it's no match for the all-out brawl that erupted as the clock wound down to zero. With just over a minute to go, UNC's Travis Burgess seemed to have thrown a pass that would move the Tar Heels close to midfield; however, it wound up in the arms of a Cardinal. RAMS OFFENSIVE LINEMAN PUNCHES BILLS LINEBACKER AFTER THRILLING GAME: 'TEMPERS GOT FLARED' Bummer. That's it. Game over. Everyone can leave. Nothing else to see. Well, any fans who did stick around saw something wild. As the Cardinals took a knee for the final time, tempers started flaring. Then they kept flaring, and really never stopped. The benches cleared , and chaos ensued. We also got one of my favorite things, which is officials trying to break up a brawl by blowing their whistles and throwing flags . Seriously? In that melee, do you really think whistling away like a London Bobby is going to do anything? SEC HEAD GREG SANKEY BLASTS ANNOUNCERS FOR CRITICIZING POOR OFFICIATING IN TEXAS-MISSOURI: 'UNACCEPTABLE' Now you don't just have a brawl on your hands. You have a brawl, a total racket and a bunch of flags you've got to go and pick up. So, did any of that improve the situation in any measurable way? No. No, it did not. Of course, with that much mayhem, there's not much the officiating can do (or would want to do), and it will be interesting to see if there's any supplemental discipline coming. The Tar Heels likely don’t need any, because they’re probably in for a rough few days. It was a bad night on several fronts for Bill Belichick's boys. Something tells me it won't be a fun week as the 5-5 Tar Heels prepare to take on Virginia next weekend.

items.summary: Johns Hopkins scientists have uncovered hidden warning signs of Alzheimer’s disease that may appear up to a decade before memory loss begins. Brain scans revealed that two regions involved in memory and emotion start shrinking before the hippocampus, the area doctors typically examine for signs of Alzheimer’s. These early changes are linked to abnormal tau protein buildup and could provide a powerful new way to identify people at risk.
